issues.fragment: offered David Burns’ “Feeling Good” to read
issues.why: В оригинале указано «книгу Дэвида Бернса «Терапия настроения»». В английском варианте название «Терапия настроения» (которое должно быть переведено как Mood Therapy) заменено на английское название книги, при этом само русское название из оригинала потеряно в процессе транскреации. Это создает несоответствие между RU и EN версиями в контексте упоминания конкретного произведения.

reviewed.note: The translator added a poetic justification ('reflect our capacity for connection') that is not in the source text.
Major semantic shift: 'shaped' implies development, whereas 'изменена' implies a pathological alteration.
Terminology inconsistency: 'thinking error' is used instead of the established 'cognitive distortion' used elsewhere.
This is a helpful transcreation. Since the book is famous by its English title 'Feeling Good', adding it in parentheses helps the reader identify the source, and it doesn't distort the meaning.

Both issues concern the handling of the book title. I rejected I1 as a 'problem' because it's a helpful addition, but I2 is a valid observation of inconsistency. They are resolved by deciding whether to keep the literal translation or the famous English title. I'll treat them as one decision regarding the book's title.

verdict.notes: The translation is of high quality, but suffers from occasional 'over-translation' (adding meaning for flow) and a significant semantic softening in the psychological descriptions. Terminology consistency is generally good but slips slightly in the exercises.
